title: Inauspicious (heidao) day
body_md:
A heidao day is one governed by one of the six harsh day-deities (Heavenly Punishment, Vermilion Bird, White Tiger, Heavenly Prison, Dark Warrior, Hooked Array). The ancients saw it as a day when energies run against the grain, prone to hitches, quarrels and delays, so they avoided launching large ventures, weddings, groundbreaking or major signings.

It is not a wholly "bad" day: routine work, study, tidying and finishing what is half-done still suit it. Treat it as your reminder to go slowly, double-check and expect less of others. This week, on an inauspicious day, review one plan instead of opening a new project.
source_ref: Hiệp Kỷ Biện Phương Thư (協紀辨方書) day-selection tradition; editor seed 2026-10

title: Auspicious (huangdao) day
body_md:
A huangdao day is one governed by one of the six benevolent day-deities (Azure Dragon, Bright Hall, Golden Casket, Heavenly Virtue, Jade Hall, Director of Fate). In the old almanac tradition it is a day when the energies of heaven and earth run smoothly and obstacles are few, suited to beginnings: signing, opening a shop, moving house, meeting someone who matters.

Auspicious does not mean everything works by itself; it is a tailwind, and you still have to row. Pair it with the day officer and check that the day does not clash with your birth sign. This week, if something has waited too long, schedule it on the next auspicious day.
source_ref: Hiệp Kỷ Biện Phương Thư (協紀辨方書) day-selection tradition; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: Day officer: Danger (Wei)
body_md:
Wei means "high and precarious", a day standing on a height and looking down. Despite its alarming name, tradition counts Wei among the favourable officers: suited to prayers, offerings, burials, settling into a new bed and long-range planning, because from a height one sees far. The day's energy asks for care, step by step.

Wei days are unsuited to actual climbing, river travel, hasty departures and reckless moves. For you, this is a day to step back, take in the whole picture and check the risks before continuing. This week, use a Wei day to examine one plan at the exact point you have been avoiding.
source_ref: Hiệp Kỷ Biện Phương Thư (協紀辨方書) day-selection tradition; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: Day officer: Settle (Ding)
body_md:
Ding means "to settle", a day when things fall into place. Tradition finds it excellent for engagements, weddings, long-term contracts, starting school, taking office and installing the household altar, because the day's energy holds what is decided and keeps it steady.

Ding days are unsuited to litigation, long journeys and anything requiring quick change, since the spirit of the day is to stay rather than move. For you, this is a day for commitment: fixing a choice you have weighed enough, paying a deposit, saying yes. This week, use a Ding day to turn one floating intention into a decision with a signature or a clear promise.
source_ref: Hiệp Kỷ Biện Phương Thư (協紀辨方書) day-selection tradition; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: Day officer: Balance (Ping)
body_md:
Ping means "level", a day of steady energy that tilts in no direction. Tradition suits it to repairing roads, levelling ground, mediation, signing even-handed agreements and ordinary routine work. The day's energy favours fairness and calm.

Because it carries no momentum, Ping is not the day for big launches, breakthrough gains or anything that needs exceptional luck. For you, it is a day to settle a disagreement, rebalance a budget, clear backlog. This week, pick a Ping day to sit down with someone you have friction with and talk it through fairly.
source_ref: Hiệp Kỷ Biện Phương Thư (協紀辨方書) day-selection tradition; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: Day officer: Establish (Jian)
body_md:
Jian opens the twelve-officer cycle and means "to set up". It is a day of beginnings and will: good for taking office, setting out on a journey, seeking learning, laying the groundwork for something new. The day's energy leans forward, like driving in the first stake.

By old custom Jian days are unsuited to groundbreaking, opening storehouses and matters of land, because the "new" energy is not yet settled. For you, a Jian day fits announcing an intention, enrolling in a course, taking the first step, while concrete construction waits. This week, use a Jian day to declare one thing you intend to do.
source_ref: Hiệp Kỷ Biện Phương Thư (協紀辨方書) day-selection tradition; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: Day officer: Open (Kai)
body_md:
Kai means "to open", a day of new doors. Tradition counts it very favourable: suited to openings, launching a shop, starting school, weddings, departures, taking office and beginning a partnership. The day's energy is bright and clear, like a window thrown open to the sun.

Kai days are unsuited to burials and anything about closing or sealing, since the spirit of the day is to open, not shut. For you, this is a day to send the proposal, speak to the person you have been shy of, publish the first post, open the new account. This week, use a Kai day to knock on one door you have stood in front of for too long.
source_ref: Hiệp Kỷ Biện Phương Thư (協紀辨方書) day-selection tradition; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: Day officer: Success (Cheng)
body_md:
Cheng means "accomplishment", a day when matters readily reach their result. Tradition ranks it among the best officers of the cycle: suited to weddings, openings, starting school, taking office, signing, moving into a new home and seeking name or gain. The day's energy is round and smooth, like fruit on the day it ripens.

Cheng is unsuited only to litigation and disputes, since a day of success should not be spent on confrontation. For you, this is the time to submit the application, launch the product, meet the decision-maker. This week, give your most important task a Cheng day and prepare it fully the day before.
source_ref: Hiệp Kỷ Biện Phương Thư (協紀辨方書) day-selection tradition; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: Day officer: Hold (Zhi)
body_md:
Zhi means "to grasp", a day for holding firm and finishing. Tradition suits it to capturing, hunting, weddings, building and repair, harvest, and above all tasks that need resolve carried to the end. The day's energy is persistent and focused.

Zhi days are unsuited to setting out, relocating and opening businesses, since the day prefers keeping to expanding. For you, this is a day to complete something unfinished, reclaim what is yours, keep a promise already made. This week, pick a Zhi day to bring one long-dragging task to a definite close.
source_ref: Hiệp Kỷ Biện Phương Thư (協紀辨方書) day-selection tradition; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: Day officer: Receive (Shou)
body_md:
Shou means "to gather in", a day of harvest and storage. Tradition suits it to collecting debts, stocking the storehouse, buying in supplies, taking on people, enrolling and seeking wealth through accumulation. The day's energy turns inward, like hauling the net back to the boat.

Shou days are unsuited to burials, journeys and new ventures, since the day prefers gathering to scattering. For you, this is a day to close the books, recover what you lent, archive documents, write down lessons learned. This week, use a Shou day to pull three scattered small tasks into one result you can put away.
source_ref: Hiệp Kỷ Biện Phương Thư (協紀辨方書) day-selection tradition; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: Day officer: Full (Man)
body_md:
Man means "full", a day of rounded, abundant energy. Tradition finds it suited to prayers for blessing, offerings, openings, closing deals, gatherings and feasts, and to harvesting what was sown. What has been planted may now be gathered.

Yet "full spills over": Man days are unsuited to burials, taking office and starting medication, since the ancients feared excess breeding change. For you, a Man day suits closing an order, wrapping up a project, inviting people to celebrate, while avoiding fresh responsibilities. This week, use a Man day to thank the people who travelled a stretch with you.
source_ref: Hiệp Kỷ Biện Phương Thư (協紀辨方書) day-selection tradition; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: Day officer: Break (Po)
body_md:
Po means "to break", the day whose branch clashes with the month branch, the most turbulent of the twelve officers. Tradition treats it as a day to avoid for almost every major undertaking: weddings, openings, groundbreaking and signings all wait. It suits only acts of breaking: demolition, tearing down old walls, decisive treatment, cutting a bad habit.

For you, do not fear a Po day; use its spirit properly. This is the moment to knock down a structure that no longer serves, bury a dead project, part ways with a habit. This week, on a Po day, break one thing you have long known needed breaking.
source_ref: Hiệp Kỷ Biện Phương Thư (協紀辨方書) day-selection tradition; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: Day officer: Close (Bi)
body_md:
Bi means "to shut", the day that closes the twelve-officer cycle. Tradition suits it to filling pits, raising dykes, building walls, burials, storing valuables and stopping leaks. The day's energy turns inward, quiet and sealed, like the bolt slid across the door at night.

Bi days are unsuited to openings, journeys, taking office, starting treatment and anything that needs expansion or welcome. For you, this is a day of deliberate rest: disconnect, sleep early, close gaps in your finances or habits, promise nothing new. This week, on a Bi day, switch off one channel that scatters your attention and keep it off until the next morning.
source_ref: Hiệp Kỷ Biện Phương Thư (協紀辨方書) day-selection tradition; editor seed 2026-10
author: human

title: Day officer: Remove (Chu)
body_md:
Chu means "to clear away", a day for sweeping out the old. Tradition marks it as good for cleansing, treating illness, dispelling bad luck, settling debts and cutting off what has dragged on without benefit. The day's energy moves toward lightening and cleaning.

Chu days are unsuited to things that accumulate: seeking wealth, weddings, taking on new stock, because the spirit of the day is release, not intake. For you, this is the day to clear a wardrobe, delete apps, end an arrangement that no longer fits. This week, on a Chu day, remove one thing that takes up space without adding value.
source_ref: Hiệp Kỷ Biện Phương Thư (協紀辨方書) day-selection tradition; editor seed 2026-10
